title: EviCare: Enhancing Diagnosis Prediction with Deep Model-Guided Evidence for In-Context Reasoning

problem.claim: Diagnosis prediction from electronic health records is an application where large language models have shown promising progress.

gap.claim: Existing LLM-based approaches tend to overfit to historically observed diagnoses and overlook novel clinically important conditions relevant to early intervention.

contributions.claim: EviCare is an in-context reasoning framework that integrates deep model guidance into LLM-based diagnosis prediction.
The framework uses deep model inference for candidate selection, evidential prioritization for set-based EHRs, and relational evidence construction for novel diagnosis prediction.
EviCare composes these signals into an adaptive in-context prompt to guide LLM reasoning.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On the MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV EHR benchmarks, the authors report significant performance gains over LLM-only and deep model-only baselines, averaging 20.65% across precision and accuracy metrics.
The authors report average improvements of 30.97% for novel diagnosis prediction.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs have enabled promising progress in diagnosis prediction from EHRs.
Existing approaches may overfit to historically observed diagnoses and miss novel clinically important conditions.
EviCare integrates deep model guidance through candidate selection, evidential prioritization, and relational evidence construction.
The resulting signals are composed into an adaptive in-context prompt for LLM reasoning.
Experiments on two EHR benchmarks are reported to outperform LLM-only and deep model-only baselines, especially for novel diagnosis prediction.

source_observation.claim: The framework prioritizes and relates evidence before composing an adaptive prompt for LLM reasoning.

interpretation.claim: Structuring task-relevant evidence before in-context reasoning may help address cases that are underrepresented in historical observations.

application.claim: For similar prediction tasks, combine model-guided candidate selection with evidence prioritization and relation construction before prompting a general-purpose model.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy transfers beyond the reported EHR benchmarks or other diagnosis-prediction settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the experimental splits, baselines, statistical testing, or exact metric definitions.
The abstract does not describe the deep models, prompt construction details, or ablation results.
The abstract does not establish clinical validity, deployment safety, or generalizability beyond MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV.
